description:
Prove the drain entitlement at the shutdown-sequence layer with a short deadline, so no server test waits out the real five-second drain.

## Background

`crates/server/tests/server_integration/graceful_shutdown_tests.rs:538` (`test_jit_server_shutdown_force_closes_a_stalled_connection_and_exits_zero`) spawns `jit-server`, stalls a connection and waits the full `GRACEFUL_DRAIN_TIMEOUT` (5 s, `crates/server/src/shutdown.rs:33`) before asserting the force-close. It took 5.32 s and is the last test to finish in the suite run.

`run_shutdown_sequence` (`shutdown.rs:152`) takes its drain deadline as a parameter and logs `drained_for_ms`. Its unit tests already pass a 300 ms deadline (`test_run_shutdown_sequence_force_closes_connections_that_outlive_the_deadline`, `:402`). A `test-support` build reads the serving process's deadline from `JIT_SERVER_DRAIN_DEADLINE_MS` (`configured_drain_deadline`). `test_the_drain_assertion_rejects_a_server_that_force_closes_early` (`:626`) uses that seam to show the drain assertion fails against a server that force-closes early.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: A unit test of `run_shutdown_sequence` with a short deadline owns the entitlement: a stalled connection keeps running for at least the deadline before it is force-closed.
- [hard] REQ-02: The serving process enforces `GRACEFUL_DRAIN_TIMEOUT` when no test deadline is configured, proven without waiting for it.
- [hard] REQ-03: The process-level test proves the wiring with a short configured deadline: a stalled connection is force-closed, the process exits zero, and the log records completion. The drain assertion is still shown to fail against a server that force-closes early.
- [hard] REQ-04: No test in the server crate exceeds 5 s on a warm target at load ≤ 10.
title: Server shutdown force-close test stays under the per-test bound
